# A part's merge kept by the rest

<!-- Generated by tools/research/registry.py; edit the matching JSON record. -->

`merge-of-a-part-kept-by-the-rest` · **recorded-checked** · theorem · F01 · [record](merge-of-a-part-kept-by-the-rest.json) · [register](../../../../RESULTS.md)

> Under a law that merges nothing, possibilities no two alike, read by a part and a rest that tell them apart, number at most the part's count times the rest's at every step: a part's narrowing spreads the rest, and a part reset at every step needs a whole no list holds.

<a id="laws--规律"></a>
## Laws

1. Where a part and a rest together tell configurations apart, k configurations no two of which coincide, their parts held by ps and their rests by es, number at most ps.length times es.length. (`Becoming.Law.distinct_within`)
2. Under a law that merges nothing, possibilities no two alike are, any number of steps on, still no two alike; so at every step k of them number at most the count of a list holding their parts times that of a list holding their rests. Narrowed to one part, every list holding their rests has at least k members; in a rest of N, the parts need a list of at least k / N. (`Becoming.Law.Lossless.keeps_apart`, `Becoming.Law.Lossless.narrowing_spreads`)
3. Where a law merges nothing and after every step a part reads one configuration, then if any configuration has another part no list holds every configuration: a part reset at every step passes what it loses into a rest that grows without bound. (`Becoming.Law.Lossless.reset_unlisted`)
4. Witness Reset: a one-bit part set to false at every step, the bit it held passing onto a kept list. The whole merges nothing, the part merges at every step, and the rest grows by one at every step, so no list holds it along any run and none holds the whole: the kept history (withHistory) restricted to the part. (`Becoming.Reset.next`, `Becoming.Reset.lossless`, `Becoming.Reset.part_merges`, `Becoming.Reset.rest_length`, `Becoming.Reset.kept_by_rest`)

<a id="conditions--条件"></a>
## Conditions

- No axiom. A law that merges nothing; a part and a rest that together tell configurations apart; possibilities no two alike; lists holding parts and rests where named. For the reset law, a part reading one configuration after every step and some configuration with another part.

<a id="does-not-show--未表明"></a>
## Does not show

- Landauer's bound in energy: no energy, temperature, probability or bath is read, so kT ln 2 is not derived; the step from a count to heat (S = k ln W, heat at least T times the entropy a bath at temperature T receives) stays a physical premise.
- That actual microscopic laws merge nothing: that is Liouville's theorem or unitarity, read by correspondence.
- Any new mathematics: this is Landauer's (1961) phase-space count, with Bennett's history (1973) as the witness.

**Standard boundaries:** No ethical premise and no Lean axiom is used. · Contains no ethical predicate and evaluates neither arising nor ceasing. · Stated for discrete steps. · A law of the formal model; its correspondence to actual systems is a separate obligation. · Names follow the structural naming criteria and are adopted only where the statement has their exact meaning; readings are interpretations, open to revision. · A relation omitted by a weaker description does not refute the fuller account.

<details><summary>Correspondence, dependencies, sources and history</summary>

<a id="correspondence--对应"></a>
### Correspondence

Landauer (1961): a logically irreversible step compresses the phase space of the information-bearing degrees of freedom, and Liouville's theorem makes the rest expand. Bennett (1973; SHPMP 34, 2003, "in a sense ... a restatement of the Second Law"); Ladyman, Presnell, Short and Groisman (SHPMP 38, 2007; disputed by Norton). The finite-rest floor is the counting shadow of Reeb and Wolf's finite-bath correction (NJP 16, 2014) and Masanes and Oppenheim's unattainability (Nat. Commun. 8, 2017). Reading (the AI's): a part that keeps itself narrow, as an organized system does, passes the distinctions it loses into its surroundings, and in a finite world it can do so only so far.

<a id="dependencies--依赖"></a>
### Dependencies

- **formal-reuse**: [recurrence-without-premise](recurrence-without-premise.md). Reuses Law.Lossless.cancel (merging nothing at a step, merging nothing over any number of steps), Law.Lossless.returns, Law.returns_iff, revisits_within and unlisted_of_new.
  - Output: A law that merges nothing keeps configurations apart and, within finitely many, returns every one.
  - Input: Possibilities kept apart, counted in a product of lists; every configuration after a step.
  - Preserved conditions: The law merges nothing. [Recurrence.lean](../../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Recurrence.lean)
- related, not a proved adapter: [least-loss-rest](least-loss-rest.md). The converse of Law.loss_needs_merge there: a loss needs a merge, and inside a whole that merges nothing a part's merge needs room in the rest.
- related, not a proved adapter: [least-loss-from-entropy-production](least-loss-from-entropy-production.md). There Landauer's floor is a physical premise (DestroysAtLeast); here its count is a core law.
- related, not a proved adapter: [rest-from-a-finite-reading](rest-from-a-finite-reading.md). The other half of LC1: rest with no least loss over a finite reading.
